transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more. 

Um, I suppose I'm here because my sleep has gotten just a little... well, completely unmoored, I guess. I'm sure it's nothing too terrible, but I thought it best to check with a professional. At first, it actually felt quite nice—I was waking up after just two or three hours, feeling completely refreshed and ready to go, drafting up all these new plans and projects. It was quite productive, really, which isn't a bad thing, right? 

But... well, lately it's shifted. Now I just sort of lie awake for hours before dawn, and my stomach gets all tight, and I don't have any sense of rest at all. Am I explaining that clearly enough? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

During that initial phase when you were sleeping only 2-3 hours and felt full of energy, did you also notice your mood being unusually elevated, more talkative than normal, or more confident/grandiose than usual?

Well, I suppose "elevated" might be one way to put it, though at the time I just thought I was having a rather good run of things. I felt... well, almost brilliantly optimistic for a few weeks there. It was actually quite lovely at first. Every obstacle that came up just seemed completely trivial to me. 

But, um... I do have to admit, and I feel a bit dreadful even saying this because I really pride myself on being polite... I wasn't entirely pleasant to be around if people didn't agree with me. If anyone questioned my plans, I'm afraid I snapped at them. I got it into my head that they were trying to sabotage me, almost as if I were the only sensible man in the room and everyone else was just dragging their feet. 

I'm usually quite even-tempered, I promise you. I hope that doesn't make me sound too terribly arrogant or difficult. Is that the sort of thing you were looking for?
How long did that period of elevated mood, high energy, and irritability last—days, or closer to a week or more?

Oh, dear... I'm terribly sorry, Dr. Smith, but I really couldn't say for certain. It's all a bit of a blur, to be perfectly honest. I know I should have kept better track of things so I could give you a proper answer. 

Time just sort of... slipped away from me when I was so caught up in all those projects. I really wish I could give you an exact number of days or weeks, but I just don't have a clear timeline in my head. I hope it's alright that my memory is a bit fuzzy on that part. Am I being terribly unhelpful?

During that period when you felt so energized and optimistic, did the people around you—family, friends, or coworkers—notice a change and comment on it, or did it cause any problems at work or in your relationships?

Oh, goodness... yes, I suppose they did notice. I'm rather embarrassed to admit it, actually. I've always prided myself on being quite dependable, you see. 

But my wife, she... well, she's been an absolute angel through all of this, but she's had to step in and take over all our finances completely. And she actually feels she needs to stay right at home with me now, just for safety, she says. It's so humiliating, really, having to be watched over like that. I do hope you don't think less of me for it. 

And as for my obligations... well, I'm retired, but I usually keep very busy. But lately, I'm afraid I've just stopped showing up reliably for my volunteer work at the museum, and the arts council. Even my friends... I've just been neglecting them entirely. I know it's terribly rude and unprofessional to just vanish on people who depend on you, and I really am trying to do better. I feel awful about it. Is that... is that the sort of information you need to know?
Right now, alongside the sleep trouble, are you experiencing a low or sad mood, loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, or any thoughts of harming yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Well... I suppose things have felt a bit... flat lately. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a very good life, really. But, um... 

I used to just love spending whole afternoons at the museum, or I'd completely lose myself in my photography, or cooking a nice meal for my wife. But recently... I don't know, I look at my camera, or think about setting up the bridge table, and I just feel... well, absolutely nothing. Except maybe just how exhausting it would be to try and pretend I was enjoying it. 

I feel so guilty about it, honestly. My wife tries so hard to keep my spirits up, and I just can't seem to muster the enthusiasm I used to have. It feels terribly ungrateful of me. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a dreadful pessimist... is that the sort of thing you mean when you ask about losing interest?

During this recent low period, have you experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices or sounds other people don't hear, or having strong beliefs—such as feeling you've done something terribly wrong or that something bad is going to happen—that others tell you aren't true?

Oh, goodness, no... no voices or anything like that, thankfully. I'm quite sure of that. But as for feeling like I've done something terribly wrong... well... 

I'm so ashamed to even bring this up, Dr. Smith. I really am. It's just... I can't seem to stop replaying this... this investment decision I made when I was feeling so energized. I just keep thinking about it, over and over, and I... I keep telling myself that I've completely ruined my wife's security. 

I've always been the responsible one, you see. For my whole life, I've prided myself on being careful and sensible. And now... I just feel like I've made an absolute fool of myself, and of everything I've worked for. I know my wife says we'll be alright, but I just feel this immense, crushing guilt about it. It's terribly silly of me to dwell on it so much, isn't it? I do hope you don't think I'm just being dramatic or feeling sorry for myself... I really am trying to be sensible about it all.

When your wife reassures you that your finances are actually going to be okay and shows you evidence of that, are you able to accept and believe her, or do you still feel certain, deep down, that you've ruined things no matter what she says?

Well... she is wonderfully patient with me, she really is. And she does show me the papers and the accounts, and she explains it all so clearly. And while we're sitting there, I... I do try to nod and agree, because I don't want to upset her or seem ungrateful for her reassurance. 

But... oh, it's so hard to admit this... the moment she puts the papers away, it all just comes rushing back. I just keep replaying that dreadful investment decision in my head, over and over again. It's like a loop I can't turn off. I just keep telling myself that I have completely ruined her security. 

I mean, I've spent my entire life being the responsible one, you know? Making sure everything was safe and secure for us. And now... I just feel like I've made an absolute fool of myself, and of that whole lifetime of being careful. Even when she says we're fine, I just... I can't shake this awful feeling that I've destroyed everything we built. 

I know I shouldn't be so stubborn about it when she's trying to help... it must be terribly frustrating for her, and for you to hear, I'm sure. I'm really trying to look at it logically, I promise. Am I... am I being too difficult about this?
